Fast BAM reading with Bioconductor-compatible arguments

Source: R/bam_read.R
bam_read.Rd

bam_read() is a multithreaded sequential BAM reader built on top of ompBAM. The interface is designed to be familiar to users of Rsamtools::scanBam(), GenomicAlignments::readGAlignments(), and GenomicAlignments::readGAlignmentPairs().

Usage

bam_read(
  file,
  param = NULL,
  what = NULL,
  tag = NULL,
  as = c("DataFrame", "data.frame", "GAlignments", "GAlignmentPairs", "scanBam"),
  seqqual_mode = c("compatible", "compact"),
  threads = 1L,
  BPPARAM = BiocParallel::bpparam(),
  auto_threads = FALSE,
  use.names = FALSE,
  with.which_label = FALSE,
  include_unmapped = TRUE
)

Arguments

file

A BAM input. Supported values are:

  • a single BAM path (character(1)) or multiple BAM paths,

  • a Rsamtools::BamFile,

  • a Rsamtools::BamFileList.

param

Optional Rsamtools::ScanBamParam (or a compatible list for lightweight use). The following fields are honored: mapqFilter, flag, which, what, and tag. tagFilter, simpleCigar and reverseComplement are not supported; setting them gives a warning and they are ignored.

what

Character vector of fields to return, similar to scanBam(what=...). Supported fields are qname, flag, rname, strand, pos, qwidth, mapq, cigar, mrnm, mpos, isize, seq, qual.

tag

Character vector of 2-letter tag names to extract.

as

Output format:

  • "DataFrame": returns S4Vectors::DataFrame (default),

  • "data.frame": returns base data.frame,

  • "GAlignments": returns GenomicAlignments::GAlignments,

  • "GAlignmentPairs": returns GenomicAlignments::GAlignmentPairs,

  • "scanBam": returns a scanBam()-shaped list-of-lists.

seqqual_mode

Controls representation of seq/qual when those fields are requested:

  • "compatible" (default): return seq and qual as Biostrings::DNAStringSet and Biostrings::PhredQuality objects, identical to those from Rsamtools::scanBam(). These are best held in a DataFrame (as = "DataFrame"); a base data.frame can carry them but cannot print them,

  • "compact": return lower-level raw list-columns for faster/lower-overhead extraction. In compact mode, seq is returned as one raw vector per read containing BAM-native packed sequence bytes (two bases per byte), and qual is returned as one raw vector per read containing per-base Phred bytes. These are not plain character strings. qwidth is needed to decode compact seq back to base letters, and qual values of 255 correspond to missing quality values. This mode is currently supported for as = "data.frame" or as = "DataFrame".

threads

Requested number of OpenMP threads used for reading/decompression. May be capped when auto_threads = TRUE. Values above 1 require a build with OpenMP (see the Installation section of vignette("BamScaleR-intro")); without it a warning is issued once per session and each file is read on one thread.

BPPARAM

BiocParallel parameter used when file contains more than one BAM. Defaults to BiocParallel::bpparam(). Set to NULL to force serial file processing. The object is used as supplied and is never modified, so it can be reused afterwards; an already-started cluster stays running with its configured number of workers.

auto_threads

Logical; when TRUE and BPPARAM has multiple workers, BamScaleR adaptively avoids oversubscription by preserving higher per-file OpenMP thread counts when possible and reducing the number of concurrently active file workers before shrinking per-file threads.

use.names

Passed to alignment object conversion. When TRUE, read names (qname) are used as object names (they are read for this even when what does not include "qname").

with.which_label

Logical; if TRUE and param includes which, an extra which_label column is returned. It is a character column (or mcol), where readGAlignments() returns a factor Rle.

include_unmapped

Logical; whether unmapped records are retained (subject to param$flag constraints).

Value

If file is length 1: one object in the format specified by as. If file has length > 1 (or is a BamFileList): a named list of outputs, one per BAM file.

Details

bam_read() is intentionally column-compatible with common BAM fields used by Bioconductor workflows and can be used in place of Rsamtools::scanBam() for the supported fields and settings; the differences are listed below.

Parallelism model:

  • BPPARAM parallelizes across files (one file per BiocParallel worker).

  • threads parallelizes within each file via OpenMP.

  • Effective total concurrency is approximately min(length(file), BiocParallel::bpnworkers(BPPARAM)) * threads.

  • If auto_threads = TRUE and BPPARAM has multiple workers, BamScaleR first limits the number of concurrently active workers to preserve the requested per-file thread count within the detected core budget, then caps per-file OpenMP threads only if a single file would still oversubscribe the machine. BPPARAM itself is never changed. A MulticoreParam that is not running is replaced by a copy with fewer workers; a SnowParam that is not running is started with only the workers needed (also when there are fewer files than workers) and stopped again afterwards. For a running cluster, or another kind of BPPARAM, the files are grouped into that many bplapply() tasks; an error then stops its whole group, and BiocParallel::bptry() returns one result per group rather than per file.

  • GCC's OpenMP runtime (the usual one on Linux) cannot start threads in a process created by fork() once its parent has used OpenMP threads, and such a forked worker (BiocParallel::MulticoreParam) would wait forever. BamScaleR therefore releases the runtime's idle threads just before each fork() in the session, so forked workers can use threads as requested, whichever package used OpenMP first. (This may also discard other libraries' OpenMP thread-private data.) With an OpenMP runtime too old to support this (GCC's libgomp before version 9), a worker forked after BamScaleR has used several threads reads on one thread, and a worker forked after another package used OpenMP threads can still hang; use BiocParallel::SnowParam() (type "SOCK") there.

Compatibility notes:

  • rname, mrnm, and strand are returned as factor columns, matching Rsamtools::scanBam(). rname/mrnm levels are the BAM header reference names; unmapped or unset references are NA (not "*"). strand has levels c("+", "-", "*").

  • Region filtering via param$which is a sequential filter (the whole file is read; the BAM index is not used). As in Rsamtools, a record is kept when its alignment overlaps a range. Unlike Rsamtools, a record that overlaps several ranges is returned once, labelled with the first of them; records come in file order rather than grouped by range; and unmapped records are not returned when which is set. As in Rsamtools, a zero-width range selects nothing, and a range on a sequence that is not in the BAM header is an error. Repeated range labels are made unique with make.unique(), one batch per range; a range given twice therefore gets an empty second batch, where scanBam() repeats the records.

  • Flag filtering uses ScanBamFlag semantics by converting logical flag requirements into required-set and required-unset bit masks.

  • Tag values are returned with their native BAM-derived type, matching scanBam(): integer-valued tags (c, C, s, S, i, I) become integer columns (or double when a value exceeds the R integer range), floating-point (f) tags become double columns, and A/Z/H/B tags become character columns. B tags are comma-separated character values. Absent tag values are NA.

  • seqqual_mode = "compact" is optimized for throughput-oriented benchmarking and returns raw list-columns for seq/qual, not ordinary sequence or quality strings. In this representation, seq contains BAM-packed nucleotide bytes and qual contains raw Phred bytes. Compact output is intended for users who want to defer or avoid full string-materialization costs; use decode_compact_seq(), decode_compact_qual(), or decode_seqqual_compact() to decode compact output back to standard string form when needed.

  • "GAlignments" and "GAlignmentPairs" output exclude unmapped records.

  • For plain as = "GAlignments" requests (no which, tags, seq or qual), the object is assembled from slots built in C++. Every invariant checked by the GAlignments validity method holds by construction, except for two kinds of record that the reader counts: a CIGAR with an op code above 8 or a zero-length op (which the validity method may reject), and an alignment that extends outside its sequence. If either occurs, methods::validObject() is run on the result, so an invalid object is never returned and out-of-bound alignments give the same warning as GenomicAlignments::readGAlignments(). Set options(BamScaleR.ga_fastpath = FALSE) to always use the validating GAlignments constructor instead.

  • For as = "GAlignmentPairs", mates are matched by GenomicAlignments::makeGAlignmentPairs(), on the read name, each record's position against its mate's mrnm/mpos, the strand, first/last, proper-pair and secondary flags. Without which, the result contains the same pairs as GenomicAlignments::readGAlignmentPairs(), ordered by the position of the first mate (pairs whose first mates start at the same position may come in a different order). With which, records are filtered before pairing, so only pairs with both mates in the ranges are returned, each once, whereas readGAlignmentPairs() returns every pair with at least one mate in a range. Ambiguous mates are dropped, and BamFile read-name options (qnamePrefixEnd, qnameSuffixStart) are not used. The mates' mcols hold the requested what fields and tags that are not alignment slots, as for as = "GAlignments".

  • as = "scanBam" returns a strict scan-like list-of-lists: without param$which, it returns one unnamed batch; with param$which, it returns one batch per range label (including empty ranges), with requested what fields and tag values under $tag. In this output mode, seq and qual are returned as Biostrings::DNAStringSet and Biostrings::PhredQuality for closer scanBam() compatibility.

Examples

bam <- ompBAM::example_BAM("Unsorted")

# Familiar scanBam-like field selection
x <- bam_read(bam, what = c("qname", "flag", "rname", "pos", "cigar"))

# Include sequence + quality
y <- bam_read(bam, what = c("qname", "seq", "qual"), threads = 2)

# scanBam-shaped output
z <- bam_read(bam, what = c("qname", "flag"), tag = "NM", as = "scanBam")
